content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] [article_no]. From this thread, I realized I can only use the basic web editor and not the advanced one. Is this a separate application, or does it work via [product_name] or [product_name] [version_no]? Thank you for your assistance.

Welcome to the forum! The availability of the extended web server depends solely on the firmware. Devices with older firmware, such as [product_name] 8.0 and [product_name] 8.1, do not support the required features for the extended web server and cannot be upgraded. This functionality is exclusive to the latest [product_name] 8.2 series.

Thanks for the greeting. Could you direct me to a resource describing how to develop a web page for my [product_name] 8.[version_no]? Also, what does [version_no]_1 mean? My firmware is [version_no]. My goal is to count four counters from I1-I4 and display this both on the unit's screen and on a web page. Thank you again!

I could provide details, but they won't apply to your setup... As mentioned, the extended web server is only available on [product_name] 8.2. Your [product_name] with firmware [version_no] corresponds to [product_name] 8.1 and FS is [version_no]. You can upgrade firmware up to FS06, giving version [version_no]. Information about FS:04 and FS:05 for [product_name] is available. FS4_1 is just a symbolic name for the first added FS4 device in a network project view.

To address your main question, your controller features an internal web page and doesn't need extra applications. You simply have to enable web access in the configuration via [product_name]. Then, open any browser and enter the controller's IP. Although the displayed page cannot be customized, it does offer functions like virtual device display or TDE display and variable status.

Hello [user_name], Unfortunately, your last post is no longer available. Let's clarify some basics. The web editor refers to software used to create websites that [product_name] 8.2 can display using its advanced web server. [product_name] 8.0 and 8.1 only include the basic web server, while 8.2 offers the advanced version. There is no basic web editor from [company_name]. From [user_name]'s response, I understand you meant the simple web server. The standard web server displays messages similar to the device or TDE screen and offers virtual buttons. It has no relation to the extended web server. Also, you don't need an mSD card unless you want to use the web pages created by the web editor with [product_name] 8.2. There is an instructional video available for using the basic web server.

Hello [user_name] and [user_name], Many thanks for your prompt support. I deleted my previous post as my question was unclear. As a complete beginner, I realize I need to review your answers before posting further. Apologies.

Attached is a basic program with four counters and a message text. Remember to enable the web server in access control. To display a message on the web server, check the relevant box in the message text properties (see attached screenshot).
Do I require an mSD card for updating the firmware? Thanks.
Yes, you do. All necessary instructions are provided on the website, which links to further information: [url].

Hi [user_name], Thank you for sharing the example—it fits my requirements well. I designed something similar and added VM variables with addresses to hold the counter values. I assumed this was necessary but now realize it's not required in your approach or even in mine. I thought it was needed for data exchange between the device and the web server. Could you clarify? Best regards and have a great weekend.
Yes, I understand your question. However, the distinction between the basic and advanced web server remains. Data transfer via the VM area is only needed for the extended web server.
I noticed in your example you seem to be from Germany. Why not post in the German language section of the forum?

I find the standard web page displaying the device screen is already very useful. Live data viewing, configuration of setpoints, direct timer input, and editable parameters are more intuitive than entering values on a custom page made with the web editor. However, the latest web editor version may offer enhanced features and capabilities.

Hello [user_name], Once I find the German section of the forum, I'll continue there. The forum software is a bit unwieldy, and I'm still figuring out its functions—it’s taking some time. Thanks very much for your tips. Regards, [user_name] (aka [user_name])
It's actually straightforward... see attachment, or follow the link...

analysis.insight_summary: Participants clarified differences between the basic and extended web server functions available in various [product_name] device versions. The main user's initial confusion stemmed from unclear documentation about web server options, leading to uncertainty about upgrading, feature access, and hardware requirements such as mSD cards. The thread reflects a need for clearer product communication, especially regarding web capabilities and setup steps across firmware and hardware revisions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for simple and straightforward tools for custom web page development for their [product_name] 8.1 device, resembling the options available for newer [product_name] 8.2 hardware. Guidance on firmware updates and deployment requirements is also sought.
